title: Relational databases
brief: Understand shared relational facts, questions and guarded changes through one shop purchase. Distinguish schema rules, atomicity, concurrent decisions, query work and durability, judge relational fit and choose a practical next route.
ownership_note: Introduce enough of each concern to choose a route; children own detailed design, formal analysis and working procedures.

title: Locks, contention and deadlocks
brief: Choose a lockable authority and a sound isolation and snapshot protocol for a decision. Design lock scope and acquisition order, then diagnose deadlocks and bound waiting without weakening the invariant.

neighbouring_ownership.transactions: Owns isolation-level reasoning; locks develops protocols and contention.
neighbouring_ownership.incidents: Owns deciding whether blocked work explains the request symptom.

title: Retries and uncertain commit outcomes
brief: Distinguish a known abort from a commit whose reply was lost. Reuse one logical request identity, reject conflicting payloads, and recover the recorded result rather than applying a purchase twice.

neighbouring_ownership.outboxes-jobs: Owns external delivery and worker identity.
neighbouring_ownership.application-sql: Owns error transport and connection disposal.
neighbouring_ownership.crdb-transactions: Owns native retry and ambiguous-result errors.

title: Storage and durability
brief: Connect logical updates to pages, buffers, retained row versions and cleanup, distinguishing reusable space, file shrinkage and write amplification. Explain write-ahead ordering, commit durability and restart recovery, and separate them from recovery after lost storage or an unwanted committed change.

neighbouring_ownership.backups: Owns restorable history and recovery reconciliation.
neighbouring_ownership.replicas: Owns copied history, progress and read routing.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-vacuum: Owns native retention diagnosis and transaction age.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-wal: Owns native settings and crash drills.
